pass_a_gloss: Said hypothetically — even with no further attendance, we gain the best by conceiving/achieving the 'how'; but clearly the so-praying is heard while yet speaking ('Behold, I am here,' Isa 58:9), having shed providence-displeasure beforehand. Declared by Isa 58:6-9 (remove bond, finger, murmur-word): well-pleased with happenings, bond-free, not counter-voting God's training ordinances, not secretly murmuring — the murmur of wicked servants blaming masters' orders, who dare not curse providence aloud yet would escape the Lord of all. So Job ('sinned not with lips/before God,' Job 1:22; 2:10); so Deut 15:9 forbids the hidden lawless word. The so-praying, profited beforehand, is fitter to be mingled with the all-filling Spirit and the heaven-and-earth-filler (Jer 23:24); through purity/prayer, with God's Word standing amid, lacking nothing, he partakes — with the mediated(?) one co-praying to the Father. For the Son is High Priest of our offerings and Paraclete to the Father, praying for prayers, co-advocating — not for his own who shun constant prayer through him, nor Paraclete for despisers of 'always pray, never faint.' Hence Luke 18:1 (judge), Luke 11:5-8 (midnight friend, shamelessness), Matt 7:7-8 (ask/receive): the good Father gives living bread (not the Adversary's stone-food, Matt 4:3) to adoption-Spirit receivers (Rom 8:15), the good gift raining from heaven (Luke 11:13 + Exod 16:4 echo).
pass_b_english: This was said hypothetically — even if nothing else attends us praying — that we gain the best, conceiving and achieving the 'how' of prayer. But clearly one who so prays shall be heard even while speaking, beholding by the Hearer's activity 'Behold, I am here,' having shed before praying all displeasure toward providence. For this is declared by: If you remove from yourself bond and finger-pointing and murmuring word — of one well-pleased with what happens, free from every bond, not voting against God who ordains what he wills for our training, nor murmuring in the hidden reasonings without audible voice to men — which murmuring, like wicked servants who blame masters' (Isaiah 58:9) orders, murmur those who dare not with voice and whole soul curse providence for what happens, yet wish to escape the Lord of all in what displeases them. And I think this is also the Job passage: In all these things that happened Job sinned not with his lips before God. On the earlier-recorded temptation: In all these things that happened Job sinned not before God. Which, commanding it must not happen, the word in Deuteronomy says: Take heed lest there be a hidden word in your heart, lawlessness, saying: The seventh year draws near — and what follows.

One who so prays, so greatly profited beforehand, becomes fitter to be mingled with the Spirit filling the whole world of the Lord and with him who filled all earth and heaven, saying through the prophet thus: Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord. Still, through the aforesaid purity and prayer, with the Word of God standing amid those encircling(?) him, nothing lacking to prayer, he shall partake — with him who is mediated by him(?) co-praying to the Father. For High Priest of our offerings and Paraclete to the Father is the Son of God, praying for those who pray and co-advocating with advocates — who would not pray for his own who do not pray more constantly through him, nor be Paraclete before God for those disobeying the teachings to pray always and not faint. For he spoke, it says, a parable to the effect that they must always pray and not faint: There was a judge in a certain city — and what follows. And before these: And he said to them: Which of you shall have a friend, and go to him at midnight and say to him: Friend, lend me three loaves, since a friend arrived to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him — and a little later: I say to you, though he will not rise and give him because he is his friend, yet because of his shamelessness he will rise and give him whatever he needs. Who of those believing Jesus' unlying mouth would not be urged to pray untiringly, when he says: Ask, and it shall be given you — for everyone who asks receives? Since the good Father gives the living bread to us who ask him for it (not the stone the Adversary wants to become food for Jesus and his disciples), to those who received the spirit of adoption from the Father; and the Father gives the good gift, raining(?) it from heaven, to those who ask him (Isaiah 58:6) (Job 1:22) (Job 2:10) (Deuteronomy 15:9) (Jeremiah 23:24) (Luke 18:1) (Luke 11:5–8) (Matthew 7:7–8) (Matthew 4:3) (Romans 8:15) (Luke 11:13) (Job 1:22; 2:10) (Luke 18:1; 11:5–8).
